title: Cap. VII: French ἐφ᾽ ᾧ as "because" vindicated — no changed tack
pass_a_gloss: So the French version used by our churches is vindicated. As for Garissoles's add-on — that the matter was fiercely disputed, but afterward the heat cooled and later writings changed tack, and so on — he is badly wrong. Placeus's view was the same throughout, and ἐφ᾽ ᾧ is better rendered 'because' (eo quod) than 'in whom' (in quo). Even so, that version does not hurt his position, for the reasons he had already put in theses published some years before that earlier manuscript existed. He had not seen that manuscript when he made the piece Garissoles calls later, and there was no reason to change tack, as the learned man puts it. No one had then objected anything by which the received rendering of the little words ἐφ᾽ ᾧ that he follows could be attacked. As for our confession, which Garissoles unreasonably triumphs over here, see what was said at p. 73 of this book. Even if there had been any such confession, it could not hurt Placeus, since it would have been made without his knowledge or consent. But perhaps enough already about that version.
pass_b_english: Thus the French version used by our churches is vindicated. But as for what Doctor Garissoles subjoins — that it had been fiercely disputed, and so on, but that from that time the heat cooled, that in later writings the tack was changed, and so on (§ XIX, p. 239) — he is vehemently mistaken. For Placeus's judgment was the same throughout, and the words ἐφ᾽ ᾧ are better rendered "because" than "in whom." And yet not even this version harms his position, for those reasons which he had inserted in his theses published some years before that earlier manuscript was made. He had not seen that manuscript when he made that piece of his which Doctor Garissoles calls later, nor was there any cause why he should change tack, as the learned man speaks. For no one had then objected anything to him by which the received version of the little words ἐφ᾽ ᾧ, which he follows, could be attacked. As for our confession, over which Doctor Garissoles triumphs beyond reason in this place, it is plain from what was said at page 73 of this book. And yet if there had been any, it could not hurt Placeus, since it would have been made without his knowledge or consent. But of that version perhaps already more than enough.
source_text: Sic vindicata est versio Gallica, qua utuntur Ecclesiae nostrae. Quod autem subjungit D. G. Sic acriter disputatum fuisse, &c, sed ab eo tempore deferbuisse impetum, in posterioribus scriptis mutata esse velificationem &c, Fallitur vehementer. Eadem enim perpetuo Placei sententia fuit, & melius verti voces ἐφ᾽ ᾧ eo quod, quam in quo. Et tamen ne hanc quidem versionem obesse sententiae suae, ob eas rationes, quas thesibus suis aliquot annis, priusquam Manuscriptum illud prius fieret, editis, inseruerat. Non viderat illud manuscriptum, cum suum istud fecit quod D. G. posterius appellat, nec cur mutaret, ut loquitur vir Doctus, velificationem causa ulla erat. Nemo enim ei tum quicquam objecerat, quo recepta, quam sequitur, vocularum ἐφ᾽ ᾧ versio impugnaretur. De nostra confessione, quam praeter rationem triumphet hoc loco D. G. patet ex dictis pag. hujus lib. 73. Quae tamen si ulla fuisset, Placeo obesse non posset, quo inscio nec consentiente facta fuisset. Sed de illa versione jam fortasse plus satis.
